title: As Trump turns 80, who are the oldest – and youngest – current world leaders?
summary: As Trump turns 80, only 16 of 186 national leaders are older. The median leader age is 63, while Nepal's 36-year-old PM is the youngest.

title: Israelis, Palestinians, Americans See War in Iran Differently
summary: Three-quarters of Israelis say the U.S. made the right decision in attacking Iran, while eight-in-ten Palestinians say the opposite. Americans are more divided.

title: Israelis, Palestinians and Americans disagree on which countries in Iran war are doing enough to protect civilians
summary: Views among Americans, Israelis and Palestinians diverge on whether the U.S., Israel and Iran are doing enough to avoid civilian casualties in the Iran war.

title: Amid Iran conflict, how do Israelis and Palestinians feel about their safety?
summary: Most Israelis, but few Palestinians, say they have access to a bomb shelter. Israelis are also far more likely than Palestinians to feel the war with Iran will make them safer.

title: About 1 in 5 Americans have used crypto; Republicans’ use has ticked up
summary: Some of the biggest demographic differences in cryptocurrency use are by gender, age and income.

title: Vance is among 1.5% of Americans who have converted to Catholicism
summary: Converts make up 8% of U.S. Catholics. The remaining 92% of U.S. Catholics were raised in the faith and still identify with it today.

title: Americans say keeping up with key news topics is crucial. But fewer say they’re highly informed themselves
summary: Democrats and Republicans broadly show similar patterns in how they evaluate the importance of staying informed about various topics.

title: Most people across 36 countries have negative views of Israel and little confidence in Netanyahu
summary: Majorities in most of the countries we surveyed express an unfavorable view of Israel and little or no confidence in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

title: Majority of new green cards have gone to immigrants already living in U.S.
summary: A new Trump administration memo could require green card seekers already in the U.S. to apply from abroad, potentially affecting hundreds of thousands annually.

title: Who do Americans think is going to win the World Cup?
summary: Most Americans say they are unlikely to follow the 2026 World Cup, though immigrants are far more likely than U.S.-born adults to tune in.

title: Federal agency X accounts are getting far more engagement in the second Trump term than under Biden
summary: Federal agencies are getting far more audience engagement on X in the second Trump administration than they did during the final year of the Biden administration.

title: Americans Are Increasingly Pessimistic About Avoiding the Worst Effects of Climate Change
summary: About six-in-ten Americans say countries around the world, including the U.S., will not do enough to avoid the worst effects of climate change. This growing pessimism is driven by Democrats.

title: Americans on what causes climate change: Human activity or natural patterns?
summary: Key takeaways: Almost all climate scientists say the planet is warming, and that this is caused mostly by human activity. But a far smaller share of the American public has shared this view over the last decade. title: Do Americans think extreme weather is worse today than in the past?
summary: Key takeaways: Recent scientific studies have found that extreme weather is becoming both more common and more intense, and many Americans have noticed. title: Worldwide, a quarter of new car sales are electric vehicles or hybrids
summary: In eight countries, at least half of all new cars sold in 2025 were electric or hybrid. The U.S. reached just 10%, well below the global average of 25%.

title: In several European countries, EU gets more positive ratings today than during Brexit vote
summary: EU favorability has risen across Europe since the 2016 Brexit vote, with a median of 62% now viewing the organization positively.

title: Right-Wing Populism in the Decade Since Brexit
summary: Since the U.K. voted to leave the European Union, right-wing populists and their parties have regularly disrupted Europe’s political landscape.
